title: Which of the seven options solves GH × H = 9K?
description: A letter puzzle G H times H equals nine K comes with seven listed multiplications. The video matches the multiplier with the units digit of the first number, which leaves two choices, then checks that the letters hide different digits. Keeko doubts that twelve times eight will do, because it also makes ninety six.
teaching_notes: One idea: the letter H is both the units digit and the multiplier, so only the options whose multiplier equals the units digit can fit. Watch for students who pick an option only because the answer starts with nine.

source: Pick the solution of GH × H = 9K from 11 × 9, 12 × 8, 46 × 2
video_script.why: The child can multiply but has not yet used the letter rules to rule options out.
video_script.substitution: Check each option against the letter pattern: the multiplier equals the units digit, the answer starts with nine, and every letter is a different digit.
video_script.anchor: the letter puzzle GH × H = 9K of the book, with its seven listed multiplications
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko sees that 12 × 8 = 96 is in the nineties and says it works. But H must be both the multiplier and the units digit, and 12 has units digit 2, not 8.
video_script.payoff_line: Twenty four times four is ninety six.

final_answer.spoken: twenty four times four is ninety six

maths_rules: GH × H = 9K: GH is a two digit number, H a single digit, and the answer is in the nineties
the multiplier H is also the units digit of GH, so the number after the times sign equals the units digit of the first number
options that match: 24 × 4 (units digit 4, multiplier 4) and 16 × 6 (units digit 6, multiplier 6)
the others do not match: 11 × 9 (1 and 9), 12 × 8 (2 and 8), 46 × 2 (6 and 2), 47 × 2 (7 and 2), 31 × 3 (1 and 3)
16 × 6 = 96: H = 6 and K = 6, two letters for one digit, so it fails
24 × 4 = 96: G = 2, H = 4, K = 6, all different, so it works
video_script.design: One puzzle and its seven listed options. Two options pass the units digit match, one passes the different letters test.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks twelve times eight works, because it makes ninety six.
<bookmark mark='same'/>But in G H times H, the multiplier is the same letter as the units digit.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Twelve ends in two, so the multiplier would have to be two, not eight. An answer in the nineties is not enough.
